original_question: Let n >= 4 and 1 <= p < floor(n/2). Is it possible to construct a homeomorphism f of the ball B(0, R) that belongs to W^{1,p}(B(0, R), B(0, R)), satisfies the boundary condition f(x) = x for every x on the boundary ∂B(0, R), and has Jacobian Jf < 0 almost everywhere on [0, 1]^n?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in the introduction: the existence, for n >= 4 and 1 <= p < floor(n/2), of a sense-preserving homeomorphism of the cube onto itself, fixed on the boundary, whose Jacobian is negative almost everywhere; with Proposition 1.2 giving the Ball-Evans approximation reformulation and Theorem 1.3 recording the proved 4-dimensional range.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the main mathematical core of the paper's target: the low-integrability Sobolev range 1 <= p < floor(n/2), the high-dimensional regime n >= 4, the requirement that f be a homeomorphism in W^{1,p}, the fixed-boundary condition, and the demand that the Jacobian be negative almost everywhere.
missing_details: The paper formulates the problem on a cube, not on a ball; the standard form nearby is a self-homeomorphism of a cube such as (-1,1)^n (equivalently, after affine rescaling, [0,1]^n).
The domain and codomain should be the same set, and the 'J_f < 0 almost everywhere' clause should refer to that same domain; your draft mixes B(0,R) with [0,1]^n.
The map is intended to be onto the same domain, not merely into it.

The nearby paper formulation is for a sense-preserving homeomorphism; while boundary identity implies the topological orientation, the paper treats this orientation aspect as part of the statement's intent.
The Jacobian negativity is required almost everywhere on the whole domain, not just on a different reference set.
The introduction immediately ties this conjecture to the Ball-Evans approximation problem via Proposition 1.2; that equivalence is part of the paper-faithful scope.
Theorem 1.3 gives only a partial affirmative result, namely the 4-dimensional case with 1 <= p < 3/2; the full conjectural range remains broader.
refined_question: Let n >= 4 and 1 <= p < floor(n/2). Does there exist a sense-preserving homeomorphism f : (-1,1)^n -> (-1,1)^n such that f belongs to W^{1,p}((-1,1)^n, (-1,1)^n), satisfies f(x) = x for every x in the boundary ∂(-1,1)^n, and has Jacobian determinant J_f(x) < 0 for almost every x in (-1,1)^n?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as reformulated in Proposition 1.2, for n >= 4 and 1 <= p < floor(n/2), does there exist a Sobolev homeomorphism in W^{1,p} of the cube whose existence yields a negative answer to the Ball-Evans approximation problem, i.e. a homeomorphism that cannot be approximated strongly in W^{1,p} by diffeomorphisms (or piecewise affine homeomorphisms)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's fixed-boundary negative-Jacobian-almost-everywhere conjecture, not at the older sign-changing-Jacobian question. In the introduction, the paper isolates this as Conjecture 1.1, then immediately records in Proposition 1.2 the equivalent approximation-theoretic reformulation relevant to the Ball-Evans problem, and then states Theorem 1.3 as the currently proved case in dimension 4 with exponent range 1 <= p < 3/2. Compared with that formulation, your draft is close in spirit but not fully stand-alone or paper-faithful because it replaces the cube by a ball, mixes incompatible domains, and leaves the orientation/sense-preserving intent implicit.
